security_audit.summary: Static findings are documentation examples, Markdown formatting, Semgrep rule templates, or CI snippets. They are not executable code shipped by the skill. One contextual issue remains: CI templates use unpinned actions, images, and package installs.

remediation.suggestion: Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs, replace latest images, and pin Semgrep package versions in examples.

remediation.issue: External command examples require trusted execution scope
remediation.suggestion: State that Semgrep, pip, jq, and CI commands need user confirmation and trusted repository access.

remediation.issue: Referenced helper scripts are not bundled
remediation.suggestion: Add the referenced script files or update SKILL.md to use commands that are present.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned CI Dependencies in Templates
semantic_findings.description: The CI examples use mutable action tags, latest container images, and unpinned package installs. Users may copy templates that accept unexpected upstream changes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited CI files directly use mutable tags and unpinned package installation. This is a copy-paste template, so users could inherit supply-chain drift.

content.value_statement: Security teams need repeatable Semgrep workflows across reviews and CI. This skill provides scan guidance, rule templates, and remediation references mapped to OWASP and CWE.
actual_capabilities: Guides Semgrep baseline scans, pull request scans, and OWASP Top 10 scans.
Maps common vulnerability classes to OWASP Top 10 and CWE references.
Provides GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and Jenkins integration examples.
Includes a custom Semgrep rule template with metadata fields.
Offers remediation examples for injection, XSS, deserialization, weak crypto, SSRF, and XXE.
limitations: Requires Semgrep and related command line tools to be installed separately.
The referenced helper scripts are not included in this package.
Semgrep results can include false positives and need human review.
It does not replace manual review, DAST, SCA, or threat modeling.

use_cases.title: Baseline Application Scan
use_cases.description: Run a first Semgrep review and prioritize high impact issues for remediation planning.

use_cases.title: Pull Request Security Gate
use_cases.description: Add Semgrep checks to CI and block risky changes before merge.

use_cases.title: Custom Rule Development
use_cases.description: Create and test organization-specific Semgrep rules for recurring secure coding policies.

prompt_templates.title: Scan a Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to run a Semgrep baseline scan on the current repository. Summarize high and critical findings first.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan only changed files against the main branch. Explain each blocking finding and suggest a safe remediation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Custom Rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Semgrep rule for this policy: [policy]. Include metadata, test cases, and expected false positives.

prompt_templates.title: Tune a CI Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our existing Semgrep CI workflow. Recommend severity thresholds, exclusions, artifact handling, and failure rules for production use.

output_examples.input: Run an OWASP Top 10 review on a web service repository.
output: Critical findings are listed first with affected files and recommended owners.
Each finding includes an OWASP category, CWE mapping, impact summary, and remediation note.
The final section separates accepted risk, false positives, and follow-up work.

output_examples.input: Create a custom rule plan for unsafe redirects.
output: Rule intent: detect user-controlled redirect destinations without allowlist validation.
Suggested metadata includes CWE, OWASP category, confidence, likelihood, and impact.
Test coverage should include vulnerable redirects, safe allowlist checks, and framework helpers.

output_examples.input: Review a Semgrep CI configuration before rollout.
output: Start by failing only high and critical findings during the first rollout phase.
Keep scan artifacts private because they can reveal sensitive code paths.
Pin external actions and images before using the template in production.

best_practices: Start with high and critical findings, then expand enforcement after teams review the baseline.
Keep scan output private and avoid publishing sensitive code snippets in shared reports.
Document every ignored finding with a clear owner, reason, and review date.
anti_patterns: Do not fail every build on the first scan without a reviewed baseline.
Do not publish raw Semgrep results to public artifacts or broad chat channels.
Do not treat a clean Semgrep scan as proof that the application is secure.

faq.question: Does this skill run Semgrep automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflows and examples. Command execution should happen only after user approval.

faq.question: Which languages can it help review?
faq.answer: It references Semgrep coverage for common web, mobile, infrastructure, and systems languages.

faq.question: Can it create custom rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a rule template and guidance for metadata, testing, and false positive handling.

faq.question: Does it include CI examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and Jenkins workflows.

faq.question: Will it find every vulnerability?
faq.answer: No. Semgrep is pattern-based. Use it with manual review and other security testing methods.

faq.question: Can findings contain sensitive data?
faq.answer: Yes. Findings can expose code paths, secrets, or business logic. Keep reports access controlled.
